title: Port colon and empty password in a URL authority
summary: Two synthetic URLs with a colon in the authority that does not start a password: a port number with no userinfo, and an empty password after the user name.
rationale: A colon alone is not a password marker. Without an at-sign the colon separates host and port, and with an empty password there is no data after the first colon to protect.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged. RFC 3986 places the userinfo password form inside userinfo, delimited from the host by an at-sign, and restricts the concern to data after the first colon; a port colon has no userinfo and an empty password has no data after the colon.

sources.supports: Applications should not render as clear text any data after the first colon (of userinfo).
